awarding_body.value: AACN Certification Corporation (the certification arm of the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses)

year_launched.note: Specific CMC launch year not consistently published on AACN public-facing pages.

eligibility.value: Candidates must hold an active, current, unencumbered RN or APRN license in the US (or equivalent in countries where AACN-issued credentials are recognized) AND hold a current adult acute/critical-care certification from AACN Certification Corporation (CCRN, PCCN, CCRN-E, or ACCNS-AG). In addition, candidates must complete clinical practice in the care of acutely/critically ill adult cardiac patients: either 875 hours in the most recent year preceding application with a total of 1,750 hours in the last 2 years, OR 2,000 hours in the previous 5 years with 144 of those in the year preceding application.

exam_format.value: Computer-based exam delivered at PSI test centers or via AACN Live Remote Proctoring. 90 multiple-choice items (single best answer). 2-hour time limit. No scheduled breaks.

question_count.note: AACN publishes 90 total items for CMC. Specific scored/pretest split not consistently published for subspecialty exams.

passing_score.value: Scaled, criterion-referenced passing score. AACN reports pass/fail on screen at exam completion. AACN does not publish a fixed raw cut-score for CMC.

fee.value: AACN member: $180. Non-member: $265. Re-take fee at same rate as initial. Subspecialty pricing is lower than the core CCRN/PCCN exams because the CMC builds on an existing AACN credential.

pass_rate_recent.note: AACN does not consistently publish year-by-year first-time pass rates for the CMC subspecialty exam.

renewal.value: CMC certification is valid for 3 years and is synchronized with the candidate's underlying CCRN or PCCN renewal cycle. Two renewal pathways: (1) Renewal by Synergy CERPs - complete 432 hours of direct cardiac patient care during the cycle (144 hours in the year before renewal) plus the required Synergy CERPs split across Categories A, B, and C; (2) Renewal by exam - re-sit the CMC exam. The CMC and its underlying credential (CCRN or PCCN) must be renewed together.

salary_context.value: BLS-reported median RN wage was $93,600 (May 2024). Cardiac-focused RNs in step-down, PCU, and CVICU settings typically earn 5-15% above the median in metropolitan US markets, though BLS does not break out cardiac subspecialty wages separately.

common_confusions.value: CMC vs CSC: CMC validates cardiac medicine (non-surgical) subspecialty care; CSC (Cardiac Surgery Certification) validates the first 48-hour post-cardiac-surgery recovery scope. Both are AACN subspecialty add-ons requiring CCRN or PCCN as a base. CMC vs CV-BC: CV-BC is an ANCC cardiac-vascular nursing certification at the broader specialty level and does not require an underlying AACN credential. CMC vs CCRN: CCRN is the AACN core adult critical-care certification; CMC is layered on top to recognize cardiac subspecialty practice.

recent_changes.note: No AACN-announced blueprint revision verified for CMC in 2024-2026 cycle.

blueprint.note: AACN publishes a CMC test plan listing content categories including ACS, Heart Failure, Cardiomyopathies, Dysrhythmias, Hemodynamic Monitoring, Cardiogenic Shock & Mechanical Support, Vascular Disease, and Pulmonary Hypertension - but consolidated percentage weights are not consistently published for CMC; treat as null.

discrepancies: certs.js lists CMC questions = 90 (canonical, kept). No verified discrepancy with AACN public pages.
